title: Amazon Business Reshape 2026: The Quiet Procurement Powerhouse Is Getting Smarter
summary: Learn Forrester Senior Analyst Jeffrey Rajamani's key takeaways from the Amazon Business ReShape event in late October 2026.
body_markdown:
I attended the Amazon Business flagship Reshape event in Nashville in late October. Two years ago, we described


[Amazon Business as a “quiet giant”](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/reshape-2024-amazon-business-is-ready-for-its-closeup/?ref_search=3516531_1782486152896) – by now, the giant is becoming harder to overlook. Eleven years after launch, Amazon Business now serves 11 million organizations across 11 markets and generates $60 billion in annualized gross sales. It is repositioning itself beyond an “office supplies” storefront by surrounding the transaction with intelligent automation, predictive customer experience and scalable innovation.


**Procurement technology market folks: pay attention.**


If there is one line that I took with me from Reshape, it is that procurement is most successful when it is invisible. Technology and infrastructure should work behind the scenes so employees can simply get their jobs done. That’s in a nutshell what describes Amazon Business strategy. One satisfied K-12 customer summed it up well: “AI should help simplify operations, support compliance, cut down on manual work. One needs the right people, processes, and AB \[Amazon Business\] to realize success.”


### **Amazon Business Isn’t An SVM Suite. And That’s The Point.**


Amazon Business does not fit neatly into the categories that procurement analysts traditionally use. It is not a conventional source-to-pay or


[supplier value management (SVM) platform](https://www.forrester.com/report/the-forrester-wave-tm-supplier-value-management-platforms-q4-2026/RES201564) , nor should buyers treat it as a substitute for comprehensive suites such as Coupa, Esker, Ivalua, Jaggaer, SAP Ariba, or Zycus. Our recent SVM research describes that market as moving toward autonomous, goal-oriented orchestration from intake through sourcing, contracting, supplier management and procure-to-pay P2P, emphasizing governance, auditability, and human control.


Amazon Business product features like real-time spend anomaly monitoring and automated purchasing insights, among others, form a cohesive control layer. They turn everyday tail-spend execution into automated policy compliance and actionable cost control. Amazon Business’ strength is in owning and improving the buying moment itself – i.e., purchasing and commerce. It begins with an intuitive commerce experience and can now wrap insights, analytics, guardrail controls, AI, and workflow around it. By contrast, traditional SVM suites offer much greater depth in source-to-contract and procure-to-pay components of the procurement process.


### **AI Moves Closer To The Buying Decision**


The Amazon Business announcements at Reshape clustered around three themes:


1. AI-powered procurement embedded in existing systems


2. A more capable Amazon Business Assistant


3. Value intelligence


1. **AI-powered procurement embedded in existing systems**


Complex enterprises should ask themselves, “Which parts of procurement can Amazon Business make dramatically easier while my SVM platform serves as the system of record and execution that provides the strategic processes, broader orchestration, and governance?”


Amazon Business is working with SVM suite vendors to bring its search and shopping experience into the tools that buyers already use. Purchasing policies, budgets, order history, and product information inform tailored recommendations without requiring the employee to leave the procurement environment. Amazon is working with SAP and other partners on a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) for B2B procurement. The UCP, announced at Reshape, is work-in-progress as Amazon Business envisions developing and scaling this foundational integration model.


Procurement systems are good at reporting what happened after a purchase. The harder problem is influencing the choice before the purchase occurs. AI-assisted guided buying can move intelligence closer to the moment when an employee asks:


*What should I buy?* Procurement pros should think about using Amazon Business for a seamless guided buying experience for tailored product recommendations, while securely exchanging data and policies from their procurement systems. The proposition is still emerging, and buyers can leverage this synergy without needing to replace their existing procurement system


1. **A more capable Amazon Business Assistant**


Amazon Business Assistant now can answer natural-language questions about spend, orders, invoices and approvals; track purchases; surface savings opportunities; and assist with payment allocation while respecting existing permissions and approval policies.


The real test for SVMs now is whether AI combines simplicity with enterprise context, authority, and control. Amazon’s advantage is that its assistant sits next to real purchasing activity. That proximity can be more useful than placing a conversational interface in front of another static report.


1. **Value Intelligence helps procurement pros prove their contribution to efficiency, policy compliance, and spend control.**


Via Value Intelligence, Amazon Business brings cost savings, operational efficiency, and purchase compliance into one view, using the organization’s Amazon Business Analytics module. Procurement has long argued that its contribution extends beyond negotiated savings, but operational efficiency and purchasing compliance are harder to translate into a CFO-ready story. Value Intelligence is a step in the connected buying process with a single, credible overview of value beyond pure cost savings.


Buyers expect technology providers to demonstrate adoption and sustained business outcomes, not merely a long list of features. Amazon has not solved the entire value-realization problem because its visibility is strongest around activity flowing through its own environment. Even so, the thinking is directionally right: value measurement needs credible proof.


### **The AWS Connection Expands The Possibility Of One Curated Catalog**


The unified storefront that AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business briefly announced at Reshape is another signal worth watching. While the announcement left more questions than answers, if it is positioned properly, it promises to present software, data, and AI products alongside physical goods in a curated experience with shared governance.
